name: Float It!

pick.label: Pick a company
pick.heading: Pick something you love and take it to the stock market
lead: When a company goes public, it sells shares to anyone who wants them, and it has to convince investors that it has a great future.
Choose something from your life, turn it into a company and float it on the stock market. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *Investors love a good story.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously this isn’t financial advice, and please don’t actually sell shares in your flatmates. It’s just for a bit of fun.

rows: What are you taking to the stock market?
What does it sell, or what does it do all day?
Three or four letters that will appear on the screens on the trading floor.
Why will it be worth more in ten years? Dream big.
One risk in the small print:
Every prospectus has to admit what could go wrong. What could?
How do you celebrate your first day of trading?

values.does: Four flatmates, one fridge and a cleaning rota that nobody has looked at since March. We produce noise, pasta and a remarkable number of empty bottles.
values.ticker: DISH (for the dishes that nobody does).
values.story: Huge growth potential: the empty bottles on the balcony are worth at least €40 at the supermarket machine, and the number grows every weekend. Also, our rent hasn’t gone up since 2019, which in Berlin makes us basically a gold mine.
values.risk: Our most valuable asset, Lukas, may move to Leipzig. Also, the landlord may read this prospectus.
values.launch: Instead of ringing the bell at the stock exchange, we bang on the bathroom door until Lukas comes out.

yours.label: Your company
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your company in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which company would you invest in?
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their company in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
